Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 3:57: And so one of the forty-eight qualities through which Torah is acquired is the acceptance of suffering (Avot, chapter 6, mishnah 6) - and the acceptance of suffering is the matter of Rabbi Elazar the son of Rabbi Shimon, who accepted suffering upon himself (Bava Metzia 84b). Along these lines, a person must afflict himself with restrictions on eating, sleeping, and pleasure, or by fasting, and the like.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 3:58: And in Tanna D'Vei Eliyahu it says that whoever accepts suffering is saved from Gehinnom and enters the Garden of Eden, in these words: this is what Scripture says (Lamentations 3:27), "it is good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth" - Elijah, of blessed memory, said: happy is he who accepts suffering from his youth, for his end shall be peaceful. From where [do we learn this]? From Job - for so his companions said to him (Job 8:7), "though your beginning was small, yet your latter end shall greatly increase." And not only that, but the suffering upon you shall save you from Gehinnom and place you in the Garden of Eden, as it is said (ibid. 36:16), "and He also allured you out of distress, into a broad place where there is no constraint, and that which was set on your table would be full of fatness." Rabbi Acha said in the name of Rabbi Yonah: his companions said to Job, even though Satan incited the Holy One, blessed be He, against you, as it is said (ibid. 2:3), "and you incited Me against him, to destroy him without cause," the Holy One, blessed be He, desired to save you "from the mouth of distress," from Gehinnom, whose mouth is narrow above and wide below, as it is said, "broad, with no support beneath it" - this teaches that Gehinnom has no foundation, neither of earth nor of stone, so that the wicked have no rest in it. And how are they judged within it? Its force tosses them like a bird, light and thin from every side, until they become like a hairsbreadth, as it is said (Psalms 49:15), "and their form shall wear away in Sheol," and it is written (Job 10:22), "a land of thick darkness, as darkness itself" - from here you learn that they stand in it like a bird standing in the air. And it is not enough that suffering saved you from Gehinnom, but it also brought you into the Garden of Eden, as it is said, "and that which was set on your table would be full of fatness" - and therefore Scripture says, "it is good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 3:59: And know that although suffering is a force of judgment for a person, and it would appear that it flows from Gevurah, this is not so, for it comes only from the side of Chesed, as it is written (Psalms 103:8), "merciful and gracious," and so on, "slow to anger, and abundant in kindness," and it is written (ibid. 103), "He has not dealt with us according to our sins," and so on, and it is written (Proverbs 3:12), "for whom the LORD loves, He corrects," and it is written (ibid. 13:24), "he who spares his rod hates his son, but he who loves him disciplines him early." And love is only from the side of Chesed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 3:60: And this is because the soul is the daughter of Abraham our father, peace be upon him, as explained in the Sabba (Parashat Mishpatim, page 95a), concerning "and if a priest's daughter marries a stranger" (Leviticus 22:12), for the soul is called "the daughter of a priest" - and in these words: "the daughter of a priest" - this is the supernal soul, the daughter of Abraham our father, the first of converts, and he draws down the soul from a supernal place - to this point. And he also explained there (page 96b) concerning (Exodus 21:8), "he shall have no power to sell her to a foreign people, seeing he has dealt deceitfully with her" - that this garment is the spreading of the precious garment from the side of Chesed, called "Eloah" - see there, in these words: the Holy One, blessed be He, marks her and seals her with a single seal of His precious garment, and who is this? The holy Name called "Eloah," and this is "as in the days when Eloah watched over me" [Job 29:2] - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 3:61: And since the soul flows from the side of Chesed, its purification too is from the side of Chesed - and if, Heaven forfend, it becomes impure, just as the priest would purify the leper, as it is written (Leviticus 14:2), "on the day of his purification he shall be brought to the priest," so the soul is purified through the fire of Gehinnom, in order to be refined, and afterward ascends through Michael, who is the supernal priest who offers up the souls of the righteous, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Chagigah 12b; Menachot 110a, see Tosafot s.v. "u-Michael"). And so they explained in the Zohar (Parashat Metzora, page 53b), in these words: afterward it is judged with several judgments. And "afterward" continues from the wording of the discourse stated there, which recounts the departure of the soul from the body, and says: afterward it was judged with several judgments, until it remained in Gehinnom in the hand of Dumah, and the body was judged in the grave until it returned to dust, while the soul was in the fire of Gehinnom with several judgments, until that time it accepted its punishment to be distanced from the place where the righteous sit; after it has accepted its punishment and its time comes to be purified, then it departs from Gehinnom and is refined of its iniquities like iron refined in fire, and they ascend with it until it enters the lower Garden of Eden, and it bathes there in those waters, and bathes in the spices that are there, along the lines of "perfumed with myrrh and frankincense" - then they ascend with it until it is offered as a sacrifice on the altar - this is what is written (Leviticus 14:2), "this shall be the law of the leper, on the day of his purification, and he shall be brought to the priest" - the supernal priest above. This soul, which was not so defiled in this world, has a remedy of this kind; but if not, "that which is crooked cannot be made straight" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 3:62: Behold, that in the end the soul is offered through the priest, and even though it enters Gehinnom and the fire purifies it, the intent is that it be refined and purified so that the power of Chesed, the white light, from which the soul flowed, as we explained, shines within it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 3:63: And we find, in this aspect, that the Holy One, blessed be He, does kindness with the soul, to wash away its stains in order to give it good reward - and this is (Psalms 139:10), "even there Your hand shall lead me" - to purify the soul, "and Your right hand shall hold me" - to give it good reward.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 3:64: And it is like the parable of a mother who washes her son of his filth, doing him a kindness - for if she leaves him in his filth, it is cruelty, and his body will be harmed; and even though the child cries and suffers, it is all for his good. So too a father who strikes his son and disciplines him with the rod does an act of kindness, benefiting his soul so that it not descend to Gehinnom - for it is better that he suffer a small pain than a great pain, which is the fire of Gehinnom, which burns continually day and night, and the soul's suffering does not rest until it is purified. And so the Holy One, blessed be He, in this world, exacts payment from the righteous and disciplines them with the rod of suffering little by little, so that they not descend to Gehinnom - but not so for the wicked, for if they were disciplined with suffering they would add transgression to transgression.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 3:65: And therefore, whomever the Holy One, blessed be He, loves, He disciplines little by little, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Avodah Zarah 4a), on the verse (Amos 3:2), "you only have I known of all the families of the earth; therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities" - they said there, this is like a parable of a man who has a loan against two people, one whom he loves and one whom he hates - from the one he loves, he collects little by little; from the one he hates, he collects it all at once.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 3:66: It follows that there are two kinds of suffering. The first is from the side of Chesed, called "sufferings of love," collected little by little, and these are sufferings that do not involve the neglect of Torah and prayer - and this is along the lines of what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Pesachim 118a), on the verse (Psalms 118:1), "give thanks to the LORD, for He is good, for His kindness endures forever," in these words: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said, give thanks to the One who collects a person's debt through his own benefit - the rich man through his ox, the poor man through his lamb, the orphan through his egg, the widow through her hen - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 3:67: And there is suffering that is not of love, which involves the neglect of Torah and prayer, when judgment flows upon him all at once - and this resembles, to some degree, the fire of Gehinnom, which purifies the soul at one stroke without giving relief and respite in between.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 3:68: It follows that these two aspects are the two aspects present within the attributes, as explained in the Zohar in Parashat Va'era - either the general inclusion of Chesed within Gevurah, or Gevurah within Chesed. What is the general inclusion of Gevurah within Chesed is "sufferings of love," where Chesed is dominant and judgment flows little by little; and what is the general inclusion of Chesed within Gevurah, where Gevurah is dominant, is suffering that is not of love - but there is never suffering in which the aspect of Chesed does not participate, to purify and refine, as we explained from the parable of the mother washing her son, and so it is written (Isaiah 4:4), "if the LORD shall have washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion" - and Scripture is precise with this Name [Adonai, spelled alef-dalet-nun-yud], and you will find good reason in my words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 3:69: It follows that whoever accepts suffering upon himself becomes a chariot for Chesed, for Chesed, who is the priest, is called "a pure man," as explained in Parashat Chukat - and this is because through suffering he purifies his soul and brings it near to Chesed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 3:70: And for this reason, one who sits in a fast is called "chassid," as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Ta'anit 11b), that it is written (Proverbs 11:17), "a man of kindness rewards his own soul" - for through the boiling of his fat and blood, diminished by the fire of the fast, he purifies his soul and refines it and brings it near to Chesed, and it is a judgment he accepts upon himself little by little, for at night he eats and is nourished from the flow of Chesed, from which food flows, as explained in the Gate of Holiness, chapter 15.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 3:71: And so any suffering a person accepts upon himself that does not involve the neglect of Torah and prayer - such as reducing his food, or sitting in a fast for so many hours of the day, as Rabbi Yochanan used to do, as explained in Tractate Keritot concerning "one who swears to do harm and does not change it" (Psalms 15:4) - such as Rabbi Yochanan, who would say, I shall be in a fast until I come home. And in the Yerushalmi, chapter "Konam" (Nedarim, chapter 8, halachah 1), it says of Rabbi Yochanan that they would fast for hours - for Rabbi Yochanan said, I hereby am in a fast until I finish my chapter, until I finish my portion - to this point. And things like this are "sufferings of love," where he does to himself what it would be fitting for the Holy One, blessed be He, to do to him out of love.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 3:72: However, this aspect - accepting suffering upon oneself from the side of love - is correct only if he has not sinned so gravely that his punishment is to descend to Gehinnom; but if he sinned in the matter of forbidden relations and the like, which is the third category Rabbi Yishmael counted concerning the four categories of atonement we explained above - for if he transgressed a negative commandment requiring suffering to cleanse it, as it is written (Psalms 89:33), "then I will visit their transgression with the rod, and their iniquity with plagues" - for certainly that suffering is in plagues, and it involves the neglect of Torah and prayer, according to reason.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 3:73: And the reason the Holy One, blessed be He, gives him harsh suffering is that the Holy One, blessed be He, has no desire in his Torah then, since his soul is greatly defiled with the filth of his iniquities - and without doubt, if suffering did not come upon him, he would know that the Holy One, blessed be He, hates him and is keeping him to consign him entirely to Gehinnom at once. Therefore he must accept harsh suffering upon himself, even though it involves the neglect of Torah and prayer - for a little Torah with a soul clean of the defiling stench of iniquities is better than much Torah with a soul full of defilement, and of him it is written (Psalms 50:16), "but to the wicked God says, what right have you to declare My statutes?" and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 3:74: And there are already iniquities that, although they are not among those punishable by karet mentioned in the Torah, our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained that they are equivalent to them - for slander is equivalent to idolatry, forbidden relations, and bloodshed (Arachin 15b), and so anger is equivalent to worshipping idols, and pride is equivalent to denying the fundamental principle (cf. Sotah 4b) - and without doubt one must accept suffering until he is purified.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 3:75: And in any case, everything a person accepts in this world, even if it involves the neglect of Torah and prayer, all of it is on the side of Chesed, and the little he accepts is considered great before Him, as it is written (Psalms 103:10), "He has not dealt with us according to our sins, nor rewarded us according to our iniquities" - for the world conducts itself according to Chesed, as it is written (ibid. 89:3), "I have said, the world shall be built with kindness." However, after the soul's departure from this world, it is judged by strict, complete judgment, without yielding even a point, as we have explained above, that the World to Come is given through suffering, as it is written (Proverbs 6:23), "and the way of life is the reproofs of discipline" - and the explanation of "the way of life" is that they are the supernal life, the life of the World to Come, requiring "reproofs of discipline" - for in order to merit that supernal delight, this certainty and this "would that" are needed, since that delight is given only to those who fear Him and are pious, as it is written (Psalms 31:20), "how great is Your goodness, which You have laid up for those who fear You," and it is written (ibid. 36:8), "how precious is Your kindness, O God," and so on, "let the pious exult in glory" (ibid. 149:5).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 3:76: And therefore suffering is needed threefold - two "reproofs," one "discipline," making three - for the World to Come includes within it two [other] levels, namely Torah and the Land of Israel, and therefore it is given double suffering, namely according to complete precision, yielding nothing. But concerning Torah and the Land of Israel, suffering is mentioned only once: for Torah (Psalms 94:12), "happy is the man whom You chasten, O Yah, and teach him out of Your Torah"; and for the Land of Israel (Deuteronomy 8:5), "as a man chastens his son," and so on - all of these are sufferings in mercy: concerning Torah, the Name "Yah" is mentioned, which is mercy; and concerning the Land of Israel, "YHVH your God" - behold, the name of mercy is combined with judgment. But concerning the World to Come, neither the name of mercy nor of judgment is mentioned, to indicate complete judgment - YHVH could not be mentioned without indicating mercy; Elohim could not be mentioned, since in the entire Book of Proverbs "Elohim" is not mentioned (except in three places), for the reason explained in the Zohar (Parashat Bo, beginning of page 39), that Proverbs corresponds to the middle line - see there. And therefore double suffering is mentioned, because he could not mention "Elohim."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 3:77: And this awakening is enough for the discerning one, to arouse his heart to repentance and to know how to purify his soul from its plagues - for a person has none more honored than his own soul, and each person knows the blemishes of his soul; and therefore, while time is granted him, let him heal himself with the remedies of repentance, which will be explained, with God's help, for each and every iniquity, the purification needed for it, before regret that will not avail.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 3:78: And having explained the need for suffering to purify iniquity, we must explain that a person must accept it out of love - and love is in two aspects. The first, that out of love for the Shechinah, he accepts that suffering upon himself - and the reason is that the Shechinah is struck through the sinner, along the lines of "a foolish son is the grief of his mother," which we explained in the Gate of Fear (chapter 9), and therefore, out of love for the Shechinah, who is his mother, he says in his heart, better that I be struck in my body than that my mother be struck.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 3:79: And further, in another aspect: when a person sins, the Shechinah departs from him, and it is so that the Shechinah not depart from him that he accepts suffering upon himself - and so they explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayechi, page 245a), in these words: another interpretation, "jealousy is as harsh as Sheol" - just as Sheol, at the time the wicked descend into it, they are informed of their sins, for what they are descending into it, and it is harsh for them - so one who is jealous demands payment for his iniquity, and reckons up several deeds, and then the bond of love is bound to him - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 3:80: And the explanation of "he demands payment for his iniquity" is that iniquity is the cause that separates the love between him and the Shechinah, as he says (Isaiah 59:2), "but your iniquities have made a separation between you and your God" - and therefore, since this lover does not want his beloved to be separated from him, he becomes, of himself, a creditor demanding his own debt, and confesses his iniquity to his beloved, and says to her: truly I have sinned against you - do not separate from me because of my sin. And since a person confesses in the court of judgment, they abstain from him, as explained in the Zohar, Parashat Pinchas (page 231a), and then his judgment is not handed over to the external forces, but the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah judge him and discipline him by the hand of holy judgment in this world, as he says (Jeremiah 10:24), "correct me, O LORD, but with judgment; not in Your anger," and so on, and so King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 54:3), "and by Your might, judge me" - and the intent is that his judgment be handed over to the hand of supernal Gevurah, which is holy judgment, and it is in mercy from the side of His mercy, blessed be He, and let it not be handed over to the external forces in Gehinnom, which is an evil strap, a cruel blow. And the demand for the debt is the demand of suffering for his iniquities in this world, in such a way that no claim remains for the accuser, who is his creditor, to collect his debt from him in Gehinnom - and he says to his soul, thus and thus you did, thus and thus you shall suffer.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 3:81: And what he said, "and reckons up several deeds," means, several good deeds to purify his soul, and so that his beloved not distance herself from him, and so that she come to dwell with him - he performs deeds within his power to find favor in her eyes, that she be reconciled with him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 3:82: And he says, "and then the bond of love is bound to him" - meaning that he accepts suffering out of love, and likewise he performs the commandments out of love of the Shechinah - and this is the purpose of love.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 3:83: And in the Zohar (Parashat Mishpatim, page 109b), they explained that repentance, prayer, and the acceptance of suffering upon oneself avail so that one not need to come into reincarnation, according to the view of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, mentioned above, in these words: "I love my master" - and with an abundance of prayers he loves the Holy One, blessed be He, and repairs his deeds, and says, "I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go free." And the Holy One, blessed be He, accepts him in that repentance and that abundance of prayers - what does the Holy One, blessed be He, do? What He was going to do - to send him back into reincarnation and have him suffer punishments in this world for what he did - He does not send him back to this world; instead, what does He do to him? He brings him near to the court of the heavenly academy, and they judge him and hand him over to the house of lashes, and the Holy One, blessed be He, marks how he was handed over to the house of punishment, and blemishes him to be under the dominion of the Jubilee until an appointed time, and afterward redeems him - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 3:84: And the reason for this may be said to be that the penitent, in accepting suffering upon himself, accepts the supernal judgment upon himself, and the attributes that purify from the blemish and its judgment - and through this he brings his soul near to Chesed, called "the end of days" [ketz ha-yamin] - and therefore he merits that his soul rest at "the end of days" and not return in reincarnation, as this matter was announced to Daniel (Daniel 12:13), "but go your way till the end; for you shall rest, and stand in your allotted place at the end of days."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 4:1: After we explained, in the previous chapter, the need for the penitent to have suffering to purify his iniquities, we saw fit to follow it with this chapter, explaining the matter of fasting, which is needed for the penitent - as is explained through the prophet Joel, peace be upon him (Joel 2:12), "return to Me with all your heart, and with fasting, and with weeping, and with mourning" - and the verse places first "with all your heart," and there is an etnachta [pausal cantillation mark] there, and afterward it says "and with fasting, and with weeping, and with mourning" - and the intent is that the essence of all, preceding the fasting and weeping, is that repentance be from the heart and from the soul.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 4:2: And the pious author of Chovot HaLevavot explained four conditions concerning the matter of repentance, in these words: chapter 4 - but the boundaries of repentance are four: the first, regret for the past iniquities; the second, that he abandon them and turn away from them; the third, that he confess them and seek forgiveness for them; and the fourth, that he accept upon his soul, in his innermost conscience, not to do them [again] - to this point. And behold, the sum of these four is what is said, "with all your heart" - for when a person performs repentance with all his heart, the four conditions mentioned are certainly included.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 4:3: And it is further possible to say another reason: sometimes a person will be sick or in a place of danger, and he contemplates repentance in his heart, that when he is able he will fast and repent - as we say (Ta'anit 8b): in the days of Rabbi Zeira a decree was decreed, and it was decreed that they not sit in a fast. Rabbi Zeira said to them, let us accept it upon ourselves, and when the decree is annulled we shall sit [in the fast]. They said to him, from where do you derive this? He said to them, for it is written (Daniel 10:12), "and he said to me, do not fear, Daniel, for from the first day that you set your heart to understand and to afflict yourself, your words were heard" - behold, it is explicit that the acceptance of the fast, even though he cannot fast, avails as though he had fasted - and this is "with all your heart."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 4:4: And fasting is needed by the penitent, for through eating the heart becomes proud and comes to rebel, as we copied in the Gate of Holiness, chapter 15, that a person rebels only through eating and drinking, as he says (Deuteronomy 11:15-16), "and you shall eat and be full; take heed to yourselves," and so on, and "and the people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play" (Exodus 32:6), and many similar cases. And the essence of the fast is humbling, as King David, peace be upon him, said in the psalm of repentance (Psalms 51:19), "the sacrifices of God are a broken spirit," as we explained above (chapter 3).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 4:5: And it is further explained in the Zohar (Parashat Pinchas, page 240a), in these words: Rabbi Abba opened, "the sacrifices of God are a broken spirit" - this verse they established: the will of the Holy One, blessed be He, is not pleased with a person's sacrifice for his sins, but with a broken spirit, though people do not know what they are saying. And thus I heard from the holy lamp [Rashbi]: when a person comes to defile himself with his sins, a spirit is drawn upon him from the side of impurity, and it grows haughty over the person and rules over him for his every desire. He comes to purify himself - at the time the Temple stood, he would offer his sacrifice, and his whole atonement depended on his regretting and breaking that spirit from within his pride, and humbling it - and this is the breaking of that level of impurity; and when that impure spirit is broken and his sacrifice is accepted, this is what is accepted with proper favor. But if this spirit is not broken, his sacrifice is nothing and is handed over to dogs, for this sacrifice of his is not the Holy One, blessed be He's, but the dogs'. And therefore, "the sacrifices of God are a broken spirit" properly - "a broken spirit," that that impure spirit be broken and not rule - and therefore, whoever breaks it properly, of him it is written (Psalms 78:39), "a spirit that goes and does not return" - let that man be in confidence that it not return to him ever - this is what is written, "and does not return." "A broken and contrite heart" - that man who has not grown haughty nor delighted in the pleasures of the world - "O God, You will not despise" - it is honored before Him - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 4:6: Behold, it is explicit that when the sinner draws a spirit upon himself from the Other Side, his heart then grows proud over him, and the essential sacrifice is a broken spirit, to break that external spirit, along the lines of breaking the shells of a nut. And at the end of the discourse he explains how the spirit is broken - through the breaking of the heart, namely, that he not grow haughty nor delight in the pleasures of the world; and through the fast he distances himself from the pleasures of the world, and thereby he breaks that external spirit.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 4:7: And they further explained this matter (Ra'aya Meheimna, Parashat Pinchas, page 247a), in the same passage, in the explanation of the verse "fine flour for a meal offering." They said, of blessed memory: YHVH is the middle pillar; His fine flour is the lower Shechinah; His light is fine flour, clean on its sides, without the blemish of darkness and without any admixture of darkness at all - for so is darkness with light: chaff and straw come first, and through Israel's iniquities darkness mixes with light. And just as a person threshes grain and afterward sifts it, sifting the food from the waste, so Israel must do with their spirit when darkness mixes into it - and the secret of the matter (Psalms 51:19), "the sacrifices of God are a broken spirit" - for thus the darkness, which is the evil inclination, is broken, which covers the spirit like chaff covering wheat, like a cloud covering the sun and not letting it shine; and at times the darkness, which is the evil inclination, covers the good inclination, which is light, it is as one imprisoned in a prison of the spirit, and likewise, when the good inclination is imprisoned in the domain of the evil inclination, so too the hosts of the good inclination are imprisoned in the domain of the hosts of the evil inclination. And at the time a person breaks his spirit in all his limbs before YHVH, what is written? "To say to the prisoners, go forth; to those who are in darkness, show yourselves" (Isaiah 49:9). But the Shechinah is fine, clean flour, in which no darkness or accusation can mix - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 4:8: Behold, this discourse explains the matter further, that through sin light and darkness are mixed, and that darkness covers the spirit like a cloud covering the sun - and this is what the verse says (ibid. 59:2), "but your iniquities have made a separation between you and your God" - being a partition. And so they said in the Tikkunim (page 109a), that these husks cause separation between the Holy One, blessed be He, and Israel, and this is the secret of "but your iniquities have made a separation between you and your God" - to this point. And so he said above this (page 108b), and these husks are a partition between Israel and their Father in Heaven.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 4:9: And since a person sins, through his iniquity he strengthens the husk and thickens the partition, making it like a partition of iron, along the lines of (Isaiah 5:18), "woe to those who draw iniquity with cords of vanity, and sin as with a cart rope" - and there is no remedy until the husk is broken through fasting, weeping, and mourning, as will be explained, in such a way that he breaks his spirit and his limbs before YHVH, as he said, "and at the time a person breaks his spirit in all his limbs before YHVH." And there is no way to break all his limbs and his spirit except through the self-affliction of fasting, whereby his fat and blood, which are the essence of all the limbs, are diminished and afflicted. And just as through eating and drinking his strength grows proud, and the chaff and straw, which is darkness, cover the supernal light of his soul, and also the spark of the Shechinah clothed within that darkness - so shall he afflict himself without eating, in order to subdue himself and separate the light from the darkness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 4:10: And especially Torah scholars must fast, in order to subdue their bodies, for the soul does not shine until the body and its powers are subdued - and as they said in the Zohar (Parashat Toldot, page 140b): come and see, at the time the Holy One, blessed be He, desires to delight in a person's soul, He strikes the body, so that the soul may rule - for as long as the soul is with the body, it cannot rule, but when the body is weakened, the soul rules - to this point. And so they also elaborated in the Zohar (Parashat Vayeshev, page 180b) - see there. And therefore one must fast in order to strengthen the power of the soul and weaken matter and its pleasures.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 4:11: And we have already explained in the Gate of Holiness that the breaking of pleasures is like the breaking of the hard shell of a nut, and it says in the Tikkunim (pages 69a-b) that the heart is like a nut, in these words: and further, the heart is a nut - whoever breaks the shell, which is the evil inclination, of him it is said (Psalms 51:19), "a broken and contrite heart, O God, You will not despise"; but the haughtiness of a heart complete with its shells, unbroken, of it is said (Proverbs 16:5), "every proud heart is an abomination to the LORD," and the Shechinah does not rest upon it - and from the side of the husks, people are called "uncircumcised of heart" - to this point.
